official.deadline_note: Two-step schedule: step 1 pre-proposals closed on 12 May 2026 at 12:00 CEST; step 2 detailed proposals close on 18 November 2026 at 12:00 CET. Only coordinators invited by M-ERA.NET may deposit in step 2.
official.application_cycle: M-ERA.NET Call 2026 - 2027 edition for the ANR; opened 31 March 2026 at 09:00 CEST
official.status_note: The ANR call page shows 'Ouvert - 2027'. Step 1 closed on 12/05/2026; step 2 is open with a limit of 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET.
benefits: The ANR allocates no aid below 15 000 EUR per partner.
For a non-coordinating partner requesting ANR aid, the requested aid must not exceed 180 000 EUR; for a coordinating partner it must not exceed 250 000 EUR.
The total requested aid for a project with several ANR partners must not exceed 350 000 EUR.

An additional 20 000 EUR per project is available for network-development activities, conditional on preparing and submitting a collaborative international research proposal to the next European Framework Programme (FP10); this raises the caps to 200 000, 270 000 and 370 000 EUR respectively.
Project duration up to 3 years (36 months).
eligibility: A pre-proposal or proposal must correspond to one and only one scientific collaboration theme defined in the call.

Minimum consortium of 3 partners requesting funding from a listed agency and eligible for it, from at least three different countries, of which at least two are EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries participating in the call.
The involvement of a single partner must not exceed 60% of the total involvement in person-months; partners from a single country must not exceed 70%.
A pre-proposal must be recommended by at least three funding agencies from at least three different countries to be invited to step 2.

ANR-eligible topics are 1 (materials for energy storage and distribution systems), 2 (materials for energy conversion), 4 (innovative functional materials with designed architectures) and 6 (next-generation materials for electronics); topics 3 and 5 are not eligible for ANR funding.
The final TRL of the project must not exceed 5 for an ANR-funded partner, and the work must be positioned in fundamental research or the first applied research segment.
requirements: Pre-proposals and detailed proposals, written in English, must be deposited by the project coordinator on the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site.
Use of the templates available on the M-ERA.NET site is mandatory; any unauthorised modification, in particular exceeding the page limit, may render the proposal ineligible.
The detailed proposal must include Annexe 1 describing the partner profiles with the CVs of all consortium participants, also in English.
Partners requesting ANR aid invited to step 2 must additionally deposit their detailed proposal on the ANR submission site, with identical information.
The scientific lead formally commits that their hierarchy has approved the submission and that the information has been communicated to them.
Where genetic resources are used, all participants must respect the Nagoya Protocol obligations, and due diligence declaration receipts must be provided by the date of final payment.
documents: Pre-proposal form (step 1), in English, on the mandatory M-ERA.NET template (closed 12/05/2026).
Detailed proposal form (step 2), in English, on the mandatory M-ERA.NET template, presenting the project as a whole with each partner's contributions, due 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET.
Annexe 1 to the detailed proposal (mandatory), in English, describing partner profiles and containing the CVs of all participants.
Parallel deposit of the detailed proposal on the ANR submission site for partners requesting ANR aid.
Consortium agreement, mandatory unless the call provides otherwise, under the conditions set in the ANR Financial Regulation.
Data Management Plan within 6 months of the scientific start of the project.
selection_criteria: Step 1 central evaluation of pre-proposals by independent international experts convened by the M-ERA.NET Call Secretariat, with invitations issued in ranking order taking account of participating agencies' budget capacity.
Step 2 central evaluation of detailed proposals by independent international experts convened by the same secretariat; proposals are ranked and selection follows the ranking.

ANR-specific objectives: significant French participation, significant opening and diversification of French collaboration networks, and ambition with a clear intention of continuity and evolution of the collaboration.
coverage: Aid of at least 15 000 EUR per partner, capped at 180 000 EUR for a non-coordinating partner and 250 000 EUR for a coordinating partner, with a 350 000 EUR project ceiling when several partners request ANR aid.
An optional additional 20 000 EUR per project for network-development activities, tied to a dedicated work package and budget and to the submission of an FP10 proposal.
Only the eligible costs of the partners that have requested ANR aid are financed; the applicable funding rate and cost types are set by the ANR Financial Regulation (eligible cost sheet no. 3).
Institutional research funding: the aid is paid to each partner's own national or regional organisation and no individual tuition, living-cost or travel allowance is established.
application_method: Register the intended project with the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site and submit the pre-proposal in English (step 1, closed 12/05/2026).
Wait for the M-ERA.NET invitation, which requires recommendation by at least three funding agencies from at least three different participating countries.
Prepare the detailed proposal in English on the mandatory template, with Annexe 1 and the CVs of all consortium participants.
Deposit the detailed proposal on the M-ERA.NET site and, if requesting ANR aid, on the ANR submission site as well, using the link and deadline communicated by email.
Validate both deposits before 18/11/2026 at 12:00 CET; increases in the requested aid between the two steps are not authorised.
official.application_route: The project coordinator submits through the M-ERA.NET Call 2026 submission site; ANR-funded partners additionally deposit on the ANR submission site using the link emailed to them.
official.citizenship_residency: No individual citizenship rule; eligibility is institutional and consortium-based, and partners subject to European Union sanctions are excluded from the call.
official.international_eligibility: Partners must come from at least three different participating countries, of which at least two are EU Member States or Horizon Europe associated countries; partners from Russia, Belarus and territories of Ukraine outside Ukrainian government control are excluded as of publication.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: For ANR funding the proposal must match exactly one of topics 1, 2, 4 or 6 of the call; proposals on topics 3 (surfaces, coatings and interfaces) or 5 (materials for environmental challenges) are ineligible for ANR funding.
official.research_requirement: An interdisciplinary transnational research project in advanced materials or battery technology, with the TRL of the ANR-funded partner's work positioned in fundamental research or the first applied research segment and a final TRL not exceeding 5.
official.duration: Maximum project duration is 3 years (36 months).
official.description: The M-ERA.NET Call 2026, the 2027 edition for the ANR, brings together more than 30 funding agencies to fund ambitious transnational research and innovation projects in advanced materials and battery technology supporting the European Green Deal and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Partners of selected projects are funded directly by their own national or regional organisations, so national and regional eligibility rules apply in addition to those of the call.
official.english_requirement: Pre-proposals, detailed proposals and Annexe 1 must be written in English; on request the ANR may provide a translation of the evaluation criteria.

not_confirmed: funding_amount as a single value - the ANR publishes a floor of 15 000 EUR per partner plus partner and project ceilings, so the recorded figure is the published minimum for a partner

tuition_coverage, living_cost_coverage and travel_coverage - the ANR publishes no statement on individual tuition, living costs or travel because the aid is institutional research funding paid to partner organisations
study_mode - no full-time or part-time rule is published
verification.notes: The ANR call page and its official annex 'Modalites de participation pour les partenaires sollicitant une aide de l'ANR' were read in full: the 15 000 EUR floor, the 180 000 / 250 000 / 350 000 EUR ceilings, the optional 20 000 EUR European-preparation supplement, the 36-month maximum duration and both step deadlines were confirmed on the ANR's own domain.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot join this call cold: step 1 closed in May 2026, so you must already hold a M-ERA.NET invitation from at least three funding agencies in three different countries before the 18 November 2026 step-2 deadline. The ANR only funds four of the six call topics, and your final TRL must stay at or below 5, so an industry-facing project aimed at demonstration is not eligible here. Budget your ANR request at 15 000 EUR minimum and remember that the amount cannot be increased between the two steps.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A French materials, energy-storage, energy-conversion, functional-materials or electronics team whose pre-proposal cleared step 1 and which needs ANR co-funding inside a three-country consortium.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your consortium still has at least three funded partners from three countries, with two EU or Horizon Europe associated countries, after any step-1 withdrawals.
Check the person-month balance: no single partner above 60% and no single country above 70% of total effort.
Confirm your topic is one of 1, 2, 4 or 6 and that the justification is already visible from the pre-proposal - it cannot be invented at step 2.
Re-check that the TRL of every French task stays in fundamental or the first applied research segment and that the final TRL is 5 or lower.
Keep the requested ANR aid inside the caps; do not plan on increasing it, because increases between steps are not authorised.
Have your hierarchy sign off formally, since the scientific lead must commit that the managing institution approved the submission.
common_rejection_risks: One or more invited partners dropping out and pushing the remaining effort above the 60% or 70% thresholds, or above 15% of total effort, which discards the whole proposal.
Applying under topic 3 or 5, which makes a French partner ineligible for ANR funding even though the consortium is otherwise strong.
A final TRL above 5 or work positioned in later applied-research segments, which is an automatic ineligibility for ANR-funded partners.
Modifying the scientific and technological objectives stated in the pre-proposal.
Adding a partner from a country that was not in the pre-proposal - only partners from already-involved countries may be added at step 2.
Exceeding the page limit on the mandatory template, which ANR treats as an ineligible modification.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Aid covers only the eligible costs of partners that requested ANR funding, at the rate set by the ANR Financial Regulation. Any partner not funded by ANR, any non-eligible cost category and any individual's tuition or living costs must be carried by the partner's own institution or other funders.
document_audit: The M-ERA.NET template is compulsory - any unauthorised change, including a page-limit overrun, can make the proposal ineligible.
Annexe 1 with the CVs of all consortium participants is mandatory and must also be in English; a missing CV set is a completeness failure.
Partners requesting ANR aid must file the identical detailed proposal on the ANR submission site as well - the link and deadline arrive by email, so watch the coordinator's inbox.
If genetic resources are used the Nagoya due diligence declaration receipt must reach the ANR by the date of final payment.
alerts: Step 1 is closed; only M-ERA.NET-invited coordinators can submit in step 2 by 18 November 2026 at 12:00 CET.
The requested aid cannot be increased between step 1 and step 2, so set the figure correctly at pre-proposal stage.

The optional 20 000 EUR European-preparation supplement requires a dedicated work package and budget, an FP10-targeted proposal coordinated by the ANR-funded French partner, and is subject to final assessment.

Applications must be approached through your institution's defence and security officer or PPST services, and projects with foreign partners are subject to SHFDS/MESR opinion - a negative opinion prevents selection.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The coordinator files the detailed proposal on the M-ERA.NET submission site by 18 November 2026 at 12:00 CET, ANR-requesting partners file the identical proposal on the ANR submission site via the emailed link, M-ERA.NET's independent experts evaluate centrally, the funder group draws up the recommended list, and each funder - including the ANR - takes its own final funding decision.
